ledger.claim: Both sides are arguing about one trip. The trip_record (EV-TRIP-00110), the gps_trace (EV-GPS-00110) and the fare_breakdown (EV-FARE-00110) each carry trip_id TRP-00110, and the trace's first fix at 18:23:40 matches the trip_record's started_at for the same trip. That satisfies the first limb of the rider's burden under POL-RD-08(a) — the artifacts describe the same trip — so this dispute is decidable on this record and is not a case of mismatched bundles.

The driver's own trace is impaired for policy purposes. Between consecutive fixes it carries a 428-second gap (18:35:00 to 18:42:08) against the 90-second limit in POL-RD-07(a), and across that same stretch a 6.9 km straight-line jump against the 500 m limit in POL-RD-07(b); the normal sampling interval is 10 s, so this is one large break, not ordinary noise. If the admissibility pre-pass has down-weighted this artifact on the same defects, that impairment is disclosed here and POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence on any fact the trace alone carries.

Because the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) and (b), a deviation may not be established on it alone under POL-RD-07(ii), and none of the independent corroborating sources that limb names is present: the chat log records no driver admission of leaving the corridor, the driver's only route words are 'going KPE', which is the optimal corridor itself, and the fare_breakdown carries no erp_gantries placing the vehicle on a road the optimal route does not use. With the trace impaired and no corroboration, POL-RD-07(iii) requires ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION, POL-RD-10(3) makes that escalation mandatory, and under POL-GEN-03 escalation is terminal and holds the disputed amount rather than collecting it.

The 2.8 km / 15.2% excess the platform reports sits just under the 20% establishment test in POL-RD-01, but that number cannot be used against the rider as if it were a clean measurement. POL-RD-07(i) requires the excess across the impaired stretch to be measured as the straight line between the bounding fixes — a reading the clause itself calls the one most favourable to the driver — and a straight line is the shortest distance between two fixes. The recorded excess is therefore a floor, not a ceiling, and the record cannot say whether the true excess crosses the POL-RD-01 threshold. That unresolved margin is exactly the data failure POL-RD-07(iii) sends to a human reviewer.

No traffic advisory covers this trip. EV-ADVIS-00110-01 is MISSING — it carries no payload and weight 0.0 — so nothing in the record names a road, expressway segment or junction on the optimal corridor, still less one with a validity window overlapping the trip. Under POL-RD-03 a traffic advisory is the only thing that exonerates a route choice, and a bare 'I took the KPE like always' is not one; with the artifact absent, no external event accounts for the distance the platform billed, and the rider should not carry the cost of a route the driver cannot show was forced on him.

The chat log will not bear the weight of a rider-requested detour either. POL-RD-04 requires the instruction to come from the rider, timestamped before the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor, identifying a place or road specifically enough to act on, and corroborated by the trace passing within 200 m of a waypoint_hint. The only rider message here is 'ok'; the message naming the KPE came from the driver; its waypoint_hint is null; and the KPE is on the optimal corridor in any event. The rider-instruction limb fails at its first requirement, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable and the excess cannot be excluded as rider-caused.

Nothing on the rider's profile raises the corroboration bar. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 — well below the 4-claim trigger in POL-RD-08 — so the extra-corroboration factor for sub-30% excesses does not apply, and that factor may never be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven. That is the only profile field the clause calls on; under POL-GEN-01 every other number on either profile, including the driver's lifetime prior_deviation_flags, is context only and cannot ground a finding.

ledger.claim: If the judge resolves the impairment against the driver and finds the excess established, the remedy is not zero. On the platform's own arithmetic the recomputed optimal-route fare is 25.68 against a charged total of 34.42, giving a refund of 8.74 — a PARTIAL_REFUND under POL-RD-02, rounded up to 8.75 and comfortably above the 0.50 de minimis. The rider asks primarily for escalation on this impaired record; this figure is the fallback if the POL-RD-01 threshold is crossed.

The rider's claim fails the percentage limb of the POL-RD-01 threshold. The trace distance is 21.2 km against an optimal route of 18.4 km, an excess of 2.8 km, which the platform's own derivation fixes at 15.22% - below the 20% figure POL-RD-01 requires. Both establishment tests must pass, and one of them does not, so no route deviation exists on this trip.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and forbids citing the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. The trace records 21.2 km - the same figure, so nothing turns on the choice - and the platform's derived deviation block returns the status 'no deviation'. The rider's '18-19 km' recollection is an estimate, not a measured excess, and cannot supply the threshold.

Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. The trip identifiers do match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, so limb (a) is satisfied, but limb (b) is not: the excess is 15.2%, not the 20% the threshold demands. The rider also states she 'was on my phone so I did not watch the route', so her account of the route is inference rather than observation, and the trace does not bear it out.

The trace contains a 428-second gap between 18:35:00 and 18:42:08 with a 6.9 km straight-line jump, consistent with the driver's explanation of phone signal loss in the KPE tunnel. POL-RD-07(i) measures the excess across an impaired stretch as the straight line between the bounding fixes - the reading most favourable to the driver - and on that reading the excess is still 2.8 km / 15.2%, below the establishment threshold. There is no qualifying excess for POL-RD-07(ii)-(iii) to operate on.

The chat log records the driver announcing 'going KPE ah boss' at 18:25:50 and the rider answering 'ok' at 18:26:14, roughly two minutes after the trip started and while still on the optimal corridor. KPE is the corridor the platform's own routing engine identifies as optimal ('optimal is KPE then ECP'), so the rider accepted the route that was in fact driven. To the extent POL-RD-04 is engaged, any excess is attributable to a route the rider endorsed in the chat_log.

The $3.00 of ERP the rider flags is a properly chargeable pass-through, not an off-route gantry. The trip_record records the optimal route as 'KPE then ECP, crossing both gantries' with optimal_route_erp_sgd of 3.00, and the fare_breakdown's derived ERP block itemises no off-optimal-route line at all, so nothing here attracts a standalone correction under POL-RD-09.

Even if the tribunal runs the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check, there is no pattern to find: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 744, far below the three-flag or 0.05-ratio test. No repeat-deviation uplift and no conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) is available on this record.

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION, and under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative: it leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status (CHARGED) and refund_issued_sgd (0.00) exactly as they stand. On this rider-filed dispute that preserves the fare the driver earned and issues no refund.

Nothing in this record triggers POL-RD-10. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, so trigger (2) does not fire; the timestamps are internally consistent (first and last fixes equal the recorded start and end, charge posted 18 seconds after dropoff), so trigger (4) does not fire; and trigger (3) is not engaged because the case is not resolved by asking whether a deviation can be established from an impaired trace - POL-RD-01 resolves it on the threshold, which the excess fails on any reading of the derived figures.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: the driver's own GPS trace records 21.2 km against a booked optimal route of 18.4 km — an excess of 2.8 km, or 15.2%, below the 20% (3.68 km) the route-deviation threshold needs — and the platform's derivation prints 'no deviation'. In an ordinary case that would end the matter; it does not here. Between 18:35:00 and 18:42:08 the trace has a 428-second gap, across which it jumps 6.9 km in a straight line — more than a third of the whole trip, and consistent with the driver's KPE-tunnel signal loss. POL-RD-07 makes that trace impaired for policy purposes, and over the impaired stretch the distance cannot be measured: 21.2 km is the shortest, driver-favourable reading, so the true excess could be larger and the 20% test cannot be decided either way. Where the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(b) and no independent source named in POL-RD-07(ii) corroborates the route — and none does: the chat log records no detour admission (the only route words are the driver's 'going KPE', which is the optimal corridor itself), the fare breakdown charges no off-route gantry, and trip_record.actual_distance_km is a copy of the same trace — POL-RD-07(iii) and POL-RD-10(3) require ESCALATE rather than a dismissal. Your case is not rejected; it goes to a human reviewer, and the disputed $34.42 is held, not collected or refunded.

To the driver: nothing here finds you detoured. Your 'going KPE' is the optimal corridor, the $3.00 of ERP lies on the optimal route with no off-route gantry billed, and no traffic advisory exists either to exonerate or to implicate you (EV-ADVIS-00110-01 is empty, weight 0.0). This escalation is a data failure, not a finding against you.

Figures used: trace_distance_km 21.2, optimal_distance_km 18.4, excess 2.8 km / 15.2%, charged_total $34.42, recomputed optimal-route fare $25.68, and — only if a deviation were later established — a POL-RD-02 refund of $8.75; that fallback is not this ruling. No referral fires: POL-RD-06 is not engaged (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 744 completed trips), and there is no unmatched billing line to refer under POL-RD-09(4). What would resolve this: the route map support could not produce, a trace that covers the tunnel, or an independent record — a charged off-route gantry, or a chat admission of a detour — placing the vehicle off the optimal corridor.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
